_what: P0.4 negative-claim register. A claim of absence, impossibility or unavailability that gates capital must carry a TEST and a DATE, and it EXPIRES.
_why: ⚑ A NEGATIVE CLAIM NEEDS MORE EVIDENCE THAN A POSITIVE ONE, NOT LESS, because it is load-bearing precisely where it STOPS INVESTIGATION. A positive claim gets checked because somebody uses it; a negative claim gets checked by nobody, because it means 'don't bother'.
_phrase_list_home: framework_integrity.NEGATIVE_PHRASES. The phrase list is itself in this register and additions are register work, not a quiet edit.

claims.evidence: ⚑ THIS CORRECTS THE BUILD SPEC. §P1.11 states E2 is sourced from Yahoo `earningsHistory` at 'one extra endpoint per ticker'. Tested 28-Aug-2026: v10 quoteSummary returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized (it now requires a cookie/crumb pair). Nothing in the tree carries epsActual/epsEstimate either — watchlist_scored holds FORWARD fields (fwd_eps_growth, eps_trend_mom_pct, rev_est_fwd_pct), which are E1 revision material, not an E2 quarter BEAT. ⚑ CONSEQUENCE, STATED NOT ABSORBED: with E2 and E3 both unsourced, D21b's STRONG (= all four of E1/E2/E4/E5) is UNREACHABLE, so the ladder ceiling stays at CONFIRMED -> NORMAL 4.5%. The 1.29x figure is unaffected because it IS NORMAL vs STARTER; HIGH and EARNED_MAX remain out of reach for a NAMED, DATED, EXPIRING reason instead of an unexamined one. ⚑ EXPIRY IS 3 RUNS, NOT E3's 6, because this is an ACCESS problem and access changes; the non-existence of a free guidance feed does not.

claims.claim: the VCI prescore artefact records no exchange or currency for its names
claims.evidence: vci_prescore_aug_2026.json records ticker/theme/name/mktcap and no venue, so a VCI name has NO venue provenance and cannot be verified against the ONT/Onterris class. QBTS, INFQ and RXRX are therefore REFUSED by the auto-verifier. QBTS is covered by the hand-declared SYMBOL_MAP (a human typed it deliberately, which is the correct escape hatch); INFQ and RXRX are not, and are named in every fetch report until the VCI pipeline records a venue.

claims.claim: 90-day analyst revision breadth has no source in this framework, so evidence channel E1 is unsourceable
claims.evidence: E1's declared definition is `90d revision breadth > 0 AND FY1 estimate up over 90d`. The only breadth fields on the screen row are `est_rev_eps_up_30d` / `est_rev_eps_down_30d` (30 days, yfinance). Measured 29-Aug-2026 over the 32-name deployable stack: 0 of 32 rows carry any 90-day revision field. A 30-day breadth is a DIFFERENT quantity, not a shorter view of the same one; substituting it would be ISA-0405's class and would CONFIRM rather than merely fail to confirm.
claims.cost: one of the two fundamental-family channels. With E2 (HTTP 401) and E3 (no free source) also unsourced, only E4 (price) and E5 (route) remain: 2 channels in 2 families, so CONFIRMED is reachable and STRONG/EARNED_MAX are structurally unreachable. The ladder ceiling is NORMAL 4.5%.
claims.expiry_behaviour: on expiry E1 reads UNMEASURED and the run must say so; it NEVER reads False. 6 runs, matching E3, because this is a DATA-MODEL gap rather than an access problem — access changes faster than a schema does.

_rule_site: `site` resolves a docstring occurrence to its register entry by MODULE + OWNER + PHRASE, for claims whose wording in the code differs from the register's canonical text. It is a resolution rule, never an exemption: the entry still carries a state, a test and a date.
_rule_not_a_claim: state NOT_A_CAPABILITY_CLAIM adjudicates prose that trips the phrase list without asserting that anything is unavailable. It is DECLARED here, in the register, rather than hidden in a stop-list inside the checker — because a stop-list is a decision nobody can review, and a future edit that turns the prose into a real claim must be noticed rather than absorbed.
